# quality


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A vault fills up with things that match many searches and answer none:
cookie banners, site footers, navigation pages, licence boilerplate.
This page has three tools for that, and all of them stay off until you
turn them on.

1.  A noise score ranks the documents most likely to be junk, with no
    labels needed. On the project’s test corpora it scores 0.988 AUC
    (area under the ROC curve, where 1.0 is a perfect ranking and 0.5 is
    chance), and 0.996 once fitted to a person’s marks. It only
    suggests: a person reviews `suggest_noisy` and then marks with
    `mark_noisy` or `accept_noisy`.
2.  A feedback log records which sections an answer cited, or which a
    person rated, once `learn()` is on.
3.  A ranker can be fitted from that log to reorder retrieval. No
    learned ranker beat plain reciprocal rank fusion reproducibly
    (`evals/RESULTS.md`), so leave it off unless it helps on your own
    collection.

## What was good

`rate` records one judgement about one section for one question.
`SIGNALS` maps each signal to a label (1 good, 0 bad) and a weight: a
thumbs up or down (`up`, `good`, `down`, `bad`) weighs 3, a section the
person read 1.5, a citation 1, and `shown`, a section that was offered
and not cited, counts as a weak negative at 0.35. `ratings` reads the
log back.

### Citations are the label

`ask` already knows which sections its answer cited. After `learn()`,
every `ask` writes them to the log through `log_ask`: cited sections as
positives and the rest as weak negatives. An answer that cites nothing
writes nothing. These rows are what the ranker and the document prior
learn from.

## The Beta prior

`doc_prior` turns the log into a per-document multiplier on retrieval
scores. Each document’s usefulness is modelled as a Beta distribution,
updated by its weighted wins and losses, so a document with little
evidence stays near neutral and one cited once does not jump ahead.
`gamma` limits how hard the prior may push, and `explore` is the chance,
from 0 to 1, of sampling from the distribution (Thompson sampling)
instead of using its mean, which keeps documents with little evidence in
play.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/vishalakshi/blob/main/vishalakshi/quality.py#L104"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Vault.doc_prior

``` python
def doc_prior(
    gamma:float=0.35, # how hard the prior is allowed to push; 0 disables it
    explore:float=1.0, # 1 -> Thompson sample the posterior, 0 -> use its mean
    lo:float=0.6, hi:float=1.6, # clamp, so no amount of evidence can bury a document
    seed:int=None, exclude_ask:NoneType=None, # ignore these questions' rows; for an out-of-fold prior
)->dict:
```

*Each document’s multiplier on its retrieval score, from a Beta
distribution over its feedback, as `{doc_id: multiplier}`.*

## Noise candidates

`suggest_noisy` ranks the documents that look most like junk and leaves
out any a person has already judged for noise. `mark_noisy` is the
lasting decision: a marked document is left out of `search`, `sections`,
`context` and `ask`. `accept_noisy` marks the current top suggestions in
one call, and `mark_noisy_many` marks a list.

The features and the `Ranker` come from
[litesearch](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/quality.html),
which computes them from the chunk store alone, and the 0.988 AUC is
measured there. The features include how often a chunk turns up among
other chunks’ nearest neighbours (`hub`), how evenly a chunk sits
between topics (`spread_chunk`), how far it is from the middle of the
collection (`off_centre`) and how much of it is duplicated in other
documents (`dup_out`). This page adds the vault’s side: the documents a
person marked, the questions each document was retrieved for
(`promiscuity`), and the rule that the score only suggests.

### Learning from marks

The fixed weights need no labels. Once a person has marked a few
documents as noisy and a few as worth keeping, `fit_noise` fits the
weights to those marks instead; held out, that scored 0.996 AUC from six
marked documents and eighteen confirmed keepers (`evals/RESULTS.md`). A
fitted blend changes nothing until `use_noise(True)`.

## The ranker

The ranker is a pairwise linear model trained on the feedback log: for
each question it learns which of two sections should rank higher.
`fit_ranker(save=True)` fits and stores it, and only `use_ranker(True)`,
a separate call, puts it in the path of `context` and so of `ask`. It is
off by default because no learned reranker beat plain reciprocal rank
fusion reproducibly in the measurements.

### The features

`PAIR_FEATURES` are signals that are already known when a section is
retrieved: its retrieval score and rank, the gap to the top score, the
words it shares with the question (raw and weighted by rarity), its
cosine similarity to the question, its length, the document prior, the
document’s kind and age, and the noise features. The method is in
`evals/`.

## Fitting, storing, switching on

Logging, fitting and switching on are separate calls, so nothing changes
retrieval by accident. `learn()` starts the log, `training_data` turns
it into rows grouped by question, `fit_ranker` and `fit_noise` fit, and
`use_ranker` and `use_noise` switch the stored models on. Whether a
ranker should be on for a collection is a question for `evals/`.
